minswaps:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the minimum number of adjacent swaps needed to reduce the damage of an S/C string to at most d, with a length-2 shortcut and a -1 return when the damage cannot be reduced enough." minswaps]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> p </REF>: char* "Pointer to an array of characters that contain 'S' and 'C' entries; the array is modified in place during the repair loop."
        <REF> d </REF>: int "Damage threshold that must be satisfied after swaps."
        <REF> len </REF>: int "Length of the array p."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: int "Returns 0 if no swaps are needed, the number of swaps if the damage can be reduced to at most d, or -1 if it cannot be reduced enough."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check whether len == 2. If true, follow the len==2 alternative flow and return from that branch; otherwise continue with the general algorithm. RESULT proceed_general]
            [COMMAND Declare local variables: i, strength=1, damage=0, temp, k=0, swaps=0, flag=0. Declare int pointer a and allocate len integers with malloc(sizeof(int)*len), storing the returned pointer in a. There is no NULL-check on the allocation. RESULT local_state]
            [COMMAND For i from 0 to len-1, if p[i]=='S', add the current strength to damage and store a[k++]=strength; otherwise double strength and store a[k++]=strength. This builds the initial damage total and the per-position strength array a. RESULT initial_damage_and_a]
            [COMMAND If damage <= d, return 0 immediately. RESULT return_0_damage_ok]
            [COMMAND Set i = len - 1. RESULT i_initialized_for_repair]
            [COMMAND While flag == 0, run an outer repair pass: at the start of each pass set flag = 1 and set i = len - 1. RESULT outer_pass_start]
            [COMMAND Within the outer pass, execute the middle loop while damage - d > 0 and i > 0, using short-circuit evaluation and the strict inequality damage > d. At each middle-loop iteration, scan left from i until p[i]=='S' by decrementing i while p[i] != 'S'; this scan has no bounds check. RESULT scanned_to_s]
            [COMMAND Within the middle loop after the scan, if p[i-1]=='S', decrement i once and do not perform a swap. RESULT skipped_adjacent_s]
            [COMMAND Within the middle loop after the scan, if p[i-1] != 'S', perform a swap: set flag=0, set p[i]='C', set p[i-1]='S', subtract a[i] from damage, then update a such that if i-1==0 set a[i-1]=1 and a[i]=2, otherwise set a[i-1]=a[i-2] and a[i]=2*a[i-1]. Then add a[i-1] back to damage and increment swaps. RESULT swap_performed]
            [COMMAND Within the middle loop at the end of each iteration, if i==1 and p[i-1]=='S', break out of the middle loop only. In that no-swap path flag remains 1, so the outer loop also terminates. RESULT middle_break_check]
            [COMMAND Repeat the outer loop while flag == 0. RESULT repair_complete]
            [COMMAND Free the allocated array a. RESULT a_freed]
            [COMMAND If damage - d <= 0, which is equivalent to damage <= d, return swaps; otherwise return -1. RESULT final_return]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: len == 2]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND If p[0]=='S' and p[1]=='C', return 0. RESULT return_0_sc]
            [COMMAND If p[0]=='S' and p[1]=='S', return -1 if d < 2, otherwise return 0. RESULT return_ss]
            [COMMAND If p[0]=='C' and p[1]=='S', return 1 if d < 2, otherwise return 0. RESULT return_cs]
            [COMMAND For any other length-2 string, including 'CC' and strings with non-S/C characters, return 0. RESULT return_0_default]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
